title: NKVD Order No. 00447 and the "Kulak Operation"
summary: NKVD Order No. 00447, issued on 30 July 1937, launched the "kulak operation" against former kulaks, criminals and other "anti-Soviet elements". It set regional quotas, including 75,950 executions and 193,000 prison sentences, which regions then exceeded; troikas judged cases without the accused present. The Hoover Institution reports 687,000 shot in the whole purge by November 1938.

uncertainty.note: Order dated 30 July 1937; the operation ran from 5 August 1937 and was extended to November 1938 (USC).

where.modern_name: Butovo firing range, near Moscow, Russia (representative execution site; the order applied across the USSR)
where.historical_name: Butovo NKVD shooting range south of Moscow, Soviet Union (RSFSR)

importance.justification: The order that organised the mass shootings and camp sentences of the Great Terror across the Soviet Union.

audience_note: Describes mass executions and arrests by the Soviet state. Totals differ between sources and cover different scopes.

related.because: The USC Shoah Foundation page says Stalin's letter of July 1937 launched the operation.

reviewer_note: Pin is Butovo, a sourced execution site (LMU page; over 20,000 shot there 1937-38), not a pin for the whole USSR, hence 4,000 km. Totals conflict: Hoover 687,000 shot in the purge, USC about 400,000 executed under the operation. Hoover dates Stalin's order 2 July, USC dates his letter 3 July. Hoover does not name the signer; USC names Ezhov.
